chunk_findings.detail: `_validate_surfaces` decides whether a section “has values” by truthiness (`any(v for k, v in vars(sec).items() if k != "none")`), so legitimate TOML values that are falsy are treated as absence. For example, a descriptor containing `[caps] mcp_tool_cap = 0` (a zero MCP-tool cap is a documented cap, not absence) is built into a `Caps` section with `mcp_tool_cap == 0`, then `_validate_surfaces` computes `has_values == False`, sees `none == False`, and raises `[caps] is empty: omit it or say none = true`. The same truthiness test also lets contradictory descriptors pass: `[caps] none = true` plus `mcp_tool_cap = 0` is accepted because the zero value is ignored, even though `none = true` and a supplied cap contradict the three-valued “absent / none=true / value” loading rule.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessreg.py:_validate_surfaces

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to verify that “all v2 sections parse,” but it includes `[meters]` and `[telemetry]` in the TOML and then never asserts anything about `h.meters` or `h.telemetry` (and it only samples a few keys from the other sections). If the loader silently ignores `[meters]` and `[telemetry]`, returning `None` for them, this test still passes, so it does not actually enforce that the v2 sections are parsed and exposed as intended.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_descriptor_v2.py:test_all_v2_sections_parse

chunk_findings.detail: The new v2 section validation infers whether a section “gives values” from truthiness (`any(v for k, v in vars(sec).items() if k != "none")`). That is wrong for the v2 facts described by the schema, because numeric/boolean values can be meaningful and falsy. For example, a descriptor with `[caps] subagent_depth = 0` (and no other values) builds a `Caps` object whose only non-`none` field is `0`; `has_values` is false and `none` is false, so `_validate_surfaces` raises `[caps] is empty: omit it or say none = true`, even though the section documents a fact. Conversely, `[caps] none = true` with `subagent_depth = 0` is not caught as “none = true and also gives values” for the same reason.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessreg.py:_validate_surfaces

chunk_findings.detail: The continuation validation treats `mechanism = "none"` as if it were a real mechanism. Given `sections = {"continuation": Continuation(mechanism="none", cap=10)}` (or `goal_command`/`loop_guard` set), `cont.mechanism` is truthy and in `CONTINUATION_MECHANISMS`, so the first check passes, and the second check’s `not cont.mechanism` is false, so `validate()` returns without error. But `"none"` means there is no continuation mechanism, so `cap`, `goal_command`, and `loop_guard` should be rejected (and a section with `none = true` should reject them too). This lets a malformed descriptor claim no mechanism while still carrying a cap, which later code relying on `validate()` may incorrectly treat as valid.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessv2.py:validate

chunk_findings.detail: The governing note says `[headless]` “keeps only a reference to an `[autonomy]` profile id” and that flags live in `[autonomy]`, with the note overriding conflicting text. The added documentation still documents `[headless]` as carrying `argv`, `model_flag`, `effort_flag`, `mcp_flag`, `max_turns_flag`, `output_flag`, `resume_flag`, `exit_codes`, etc., and `test_all_v2_sections_parse` asserts that a descriptor with `[headless] argv = ["acme", "-p"]`, `model_flag = "--model"`, and `exit_codes = { "1" = "error" }` parses successfully. Under the amended ownership, those keys should be rejected in `[headless]` or placed in the `[autonomy]` profile; the change instead accepts and documents them as headless fields.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/adding-a-harness.md:95 / tests/test_harness_descriptor_v2.py:40

chunk_findings.detail: `check_table` only treats a missing `mechanism` key as `none`, and `validate` only checks `continuation.mechanism` when it is truthy. Therefore an explicit empty-string mechanism is accepted. For example, a raw `[continuation]` table with `mechanism = ""` and `cap = 3` (or `goal_command`/`loop_guard` set) passes `check_table`: `keys` contains `cap`, but `table.get("mechanism", "none")` returns `""`, not `"none"`, so the “cap/goal_command/loop_guard need a mechanism other than none” check is skipped. Then `validate` also skips the enum check because `cont.mechanism` is falsy. The result is that `Continuation(mechanism="", cap=3)` is accepted even though `""` is not in `CONTINUATION_MECHANISMS` and a cap/goal/loop value is supposed to require a real mechanism.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessv2.py:check_table

chunk_findings.detail: The new descriptor-v2 table lists the `[caps]` keys as `mcp_tools`, `instructions_bytes`, and `subagent_depth`, but the v2 `Caps` section in this change uses `mcp_tool_cap` (and analogous `*_cap` keys) for those limits. Because the intent says descriptor v2 sections are strictly loaded, a user who writes a descriptor exactly as documented, e.g. `[caps]` with `mcp_tools = 5`, will be rejected for an unknown key instead of getting the documented cap. The documentation should name the actual strict schema keys.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/adding-a-harness.md:95

chunk_findings.detail: The previous finding still holds: the test includes `[meters]` and `[telemetry]` in the TOML, but the assertions never touch `h.meters` or `h.telemetry`. Given the same descriptor, if `parse` silently ignores those two sections (or puts them in `h.reserved`) and leaves `h.meters`/`h.telemetry` as `None`, the test still passes. The test also does not assert `h.headless.autonomy == "yolo"` or anything about `h.autonomy.profiles/files`, so a loader that moves the `headless.autonomy` reference out of `[headless]`—contrary to the governing note—would also pass.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_descriptor_v2.py:test_all_v2_sections_parse

chunk_findings.detail: The test only loops over `harnessreg.load()` and never asserts that the result is non-empty. If a path/environment regression causes `harnessreg.load()` to return an empty list, the loop body never runs and the test passes, so it does not actually verify that shipped descriptors were loaded.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_descriptor_v2.py:test_shipped_descriptors_still_load_with_v2_not_verified
